source.title: Universal Redundancies in Time Series Foundation Models
source.authors: Anthony Bao; Venkata Hasith Vattikuti; Jeffrey Lai; William Gilpin

record.tranche_reason: The study tests analogous component-ablation robustness in time-series foundation models, a different model setting from the language-model claim. It reports forecast outcomes after ablation but does not measure whether downstream components change their outputs to compensate.
record.gate_note: The paper directly ablates model components and reports forecast metrics, so those outcomes are recorded. They measure forecast performance after ablation, not downstream-component changes or restoration relative to a component’s direct effect. The paper’s citations and discussion of self-repair in language models are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: The study zero-ablates heads, MLPs and layers in time-series foundation models and reports only forecast metrics (MASE, CRPS, Spearman distance) after ablation. It never compares an ablated component's direct effect with its total effect, and never measures whether downstream components change their output. Its results therefore show redundancy or robustness, not compensation. It cites McGrath et al. (2023) and says it 'establishes and explores the same phenomenon for TSFMs', but its own data cannot bear on any version of the claim. That makes this discussion, not a test; the record's 'tests/T3' is wrong.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that leading TSFMs have redundant intermediate-layer components. They say a data-independent stable-rank head-pruning strategy preserves forecast structure under heavy ablation, and that sharp heads drive context parroting and seasonality bias. They frame this as the same phenomenon as LLM head redundancy and the Hydra effect, but measure no downstream compensation.
record.recipe_differences: The study zero-ablates selected attention heads, MLPs, and layers in time-series foundation models and evaluates forecast similarity or forecasting metrics. It does not measure the direct component effect against subsequent downstream compensation.
record.method_sensitivity: Sensitivity varies by model architecture and component depth: early and late layers are generally more important than middle layers; Chronos Bolt is especially resilient to MLP ablation; Toto is more sensitive. The paper also reports that results can vary by dataset, with Moirai 1.1 notably affected by a few datasets.

fits_no_version.finding: Across Chronos 2, TimesFM 2.5, Toto and Chronos Bolt, zero-ablating 24–43% of heads (plus some MLPs) chosen by stable rank raises GIFT-Eval MASE by 3.5–10.7%. Middle layers are the most ablatable; random head selection destroys forecast structure.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Transformer time-series foundation models contain redundant middle-layer components whose zero-ablation causes small aggregate forecast degradation.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306, 2026
record.problems: The reported ablation-performance results do not measure downstream component changes or compare the ablation’s total effect with the ablated component’s direct effect. No uncertainty estimates are stated for the Table 1 metrics.
record.rows_left_out: Figure-only ablation results and per-dataset heatmaps were not extracted; they do not directly measure downstream self-repair. Other layer-ablation and forecast examples are omitted because the kept table rows already record the main numeric ablation-performance findings.

untested.parts: There is no measurement of later attention layers changing their output after an earlier layer is ablated. Whole-layer ablation results (Fig. 2, Table 5) report only forecast degradation.
Late-MLP erasure and its change under upstream ablation are not measured.
Models are time-series models, not language models. Head ablations report forecast metrics, not partial compensation relative to direct effect.
Per-dataset heatmaps show variation and some improvements under ablation, but these are not compensation fractions or overcorrection of a direct effect.
Sharp heads and induction heads are characterised as drivers of parroting, not as self-repair mechanisms. No backup heads, LayerNorm rescaling or anti-erasure neurons are tested.
Only zero ablation is used, and self-repair is not measured under any ablation type.
The study does not test whether ablation-based importance misstates component function.

record.verdict_notes: Redundancy (small total effect of ablation) is conflated in the paper with self-repair (downstream compensation of a component's direct effect). The DLA residual-stream analysis (Fig. 1, Fig. 26) shows middle layers have small direct contributions in Chronos. That is evidence of low direct effect, not of compensation.

versions.untested_parts: Does not measure whether later attention layers change their outputs or restore a prediction after an attention-layer ablation.
Does not measure late-MLP effects on a maximum-likelihood token or their change after earlier-component ablation.
Tests time-series forecasts, not self-repair on the full language-model output distribution or general text.
Dataset-level variation in forecast metrics is not a measurement of prompt-level variation or overcorrection in self-repair.
Does not test backup heads, copy-suppression heads, final LayerNorm rescaling, or anti-erasure neurons as self-repair mechanisms.
Uses zero ablation, but does not measure self-repair under zero or on-distribution ablations.
Does not test whether ablation-based importance scores misstate component function because of self-repair.

rows.subject: Chronos 2
rows.operation_detail: Zero-ablated 24% of heads and 2 MLPs using the intrinsic head-pruning strategy.
rows.measure: Percent change in MASE geometric mean
rows.note: The reported forecast metric does not show whether downstream components compensate.
rows.check: The links and states are correct: these are aggregate forecast-metric changes under the study's own stable-rank pruning, with no measure of downstream compensation. The reader's relation 'tests' and tranche T3 should be 'discusses' and T6. Note that r12 (Chronos Bolt CRPS +0.19%) comes from the same ablation as r11 (MASE +4.24%), so metric choice changes how robust the model looks.
